title: Enforce one fail-closed outbound Nostr admission layer for every Bahia publisher
observed_failure: On 2026-09-27 relay amplification recurred: projector-local dedupe and backoff did not bound DNS reconciliation retries, snapshot repair, reconnect replay, or independently packaged Bahia-derived binaries.
invariants: Every EVENT frame leaves through an approved gateway admitted by the process-wide nostrout controller immediately before the frame.
Budgets are process-wide, partitioned by lane, bounded in aggregate and per relay, and have no unlimited mode.
Relay rate-limit feedback opens a shared jittered circuit breaker; a stale success cannot close a newer circuit.
Duplicate suppression is per event and relay; concurrent duplicates are refused.
Operator results and tombstones keep reserved priority capacity that bulk and state traffic cannot consume.
Multi-event security operations are admitted all-or-none before their first irreversible step and paced rather than rejected mid-operation.
Queues, operation sizes, operation lifetimes, receipt caches, relay identities, active publications, and outbox retry lifetimes are bounded with explicit overflow errors.
A file-backed kill switch stops every publication, including NIP-46 signer requests, without restart; an unreadable file fails closed.
A type-aware static guard rejects new raw publication sites and isolated production controllers.
out_of_scope: Signer, key, ACL, grant, binding, or custody changes
Transactional coalescing of pending replaceable events by coordinate
Protocol-level atomic visibility of multi-event operations across relays
